text:
Sophia: Heads up 0000000000running HF->Redwood conversion for the new chat model. Our evals show token-level misalignment: answers are shifted and some spans don't line up in QA.
Kevin: Most likely normalization / pretokenizer mismatch. HF checkpoints sometimes use 'NFC' vs 'NFKC' and pretokenizers like byte-fallback vs metaspace change token boundaries.
Amanda: Quick repro script showed NBSP and soft-hyphen causing split differences. Also saw emoji sequences explode into 3-4 tokens after conversion.
Jonathan: Example I saw locally (different markers):
```
# original HF (sentencepiece-like)
orig.encode("▁this is a test") -> ['▁this', '▁is', '▁a', '▁test']
# converted wrapper (metaspace lost)
conv.encode(" this is a test") -> ['this', ' is', ' a', ' test']
# note the missing leading metaspace token which breaks our template concat
```
Sophia: That missing leading marker breaks the chat system prefix logic we use (system + user + assistant concatenation). Our playback tests show the system prompt merging with user text.
Kevin: Also check `add_prefix_space` behavior. GPT2-style wrappers rely on an explicit flag; if it's unset, token offsets shift. Conversion tools sometimes preserve special_tokens_map but forget to set the runtime flag.
Amanda: Another gotcha: HF tokenizers with `byte_fallback` can split complex ligatures or combined emoji, while metaspace keeps them intact as single tokens in many cases. That changes sequence lengths and batching behavior.
infra-bot: rw-convert log snippet:
```
rw-convert --from hf --tokenizer /tmp/tok.json --out /rw/models/x
INFO: pre_tokenizer=byte_fallback
INFO: normalization=NFC
INFO: special_tokens preserved
```
Jonathan: We also found control-char handling differences (ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE, LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK). HF sometimes normalizes them away depending on the normalization step; runtime kept them and tokenized differently.
Sophia: Impact on evals: perplexity looked similar, but exact-match and F1 on our QA set dropped by ~5 points — classic tokenization misalignment.
Amanda: Short checklist for conversions (recommend adding to rw-convert):
- assert normalization mode (NFC / NFKC / NFKD) matches source
- assert pre_tokenizer (byte_fallback vs metaspace) and patch if needed
- explicitly set add_prefix_space if original uses GPT2-like behavior
- compare token counts on a 2k prompt sample and print top diffs
- sanity-check special token roundtrip for system/user/bos/eos
Kevin: I'll add a smoke-test that compares tokenization on a canonical prompt set and fails conversion if token count or first-token markers differ.
Amanda: I'll run the 2k diffs now and post the top 20 mismatches (NBSP, soft-hyphen, emoji clusters, zero-width chars).
Sophia: Blocking model canary until we have the smoke-test and a remediation path. For quick mitigations, inserting a leading space into the system string helped in one sample (" System: ..."). Not ideal but useful in a pinch.
Jonathan: Also consider adding an automatic normalization step in the runtime that mirrors the tokenizer's normalization so playback/embeddings paths match.
Sophia: Thanks all. Ping me if you want the token-diff script, I'll drop it in eng-ml.
Amanda: starting run 3k prompts queued, will update with CSV of diff counts.
Kevin: Once we have the smoke-test, infra can gate canaries on it.
Sophia: Nice. :seedling:
